entities.name: Reducto
entities.how_described: 本集介绍 Reducto 是一个智能体化文档平台，位于模型与非结构化企业数据之间的层，三年处理超 30 亿份文档，客户包括 Harvey、ScaleAI。

evidence.quote: So I'm Abi and I work on product here at Reducto.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And before I dive in right away, I wanted to give you guys some more context on what Reducto is.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And so Reducto is a layer that sits between your model and that data.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: At Reducto, we've been building tools that basically automate end-to-end document work through pipelines.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: One thing that I noticed early on was that any of the users, especially our sales team at Reducto, was spending all their time in configuration instead of outcomes.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: For example, a common use case with Reducto is to route our classify endpoint that classifies documents into an extract node.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: In our system, or with Reducto, failures carry information.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And by using Reducto for the document layer, we can guarantee accurate parses and extractions for parts of the pipeline that we can't trust agents with.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And so one thing that kind of told me that we were doing something right with these improvements is I never explicitly told the sales team to use the agent to build pipelines, but rather I just exposed it in our Claude enterprise as reducto tools.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And also, we're at Reducto's at a booth P8.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

entities.name: 智能体 (agent)
entities.how_described: 本集核心主线：智能体犯错时非常自信且无人能察觉，架构设计应围绕『谁为智能体的错误买单』来组织，把判断权留在人手里。

evidence.quote: We're building agent-first software.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: But she asked me, what is agent-first software?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Building a really good harness, building a really good API, writing or iterating on prompts, all of these don't really land on the agent being put first.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Agent-first software is inherently an architecture problem.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And so I think that structure, that architecture really comes down to one question and that is who pays for the agent being wrong?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So you have auto mode to start where you optimize for autonomy, you write a prompt and you let the agent do whatever it wants.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: This is where you optimize the human interface, give the user all the knobs, and then you bolt on an agent that can't really do much, which is basically just a chatbot experience.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And the agent's capability within the product as well.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And lastly, the bucket that I think wins here is agent experience in service of the user.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: This is where the agent's capabilities are structured to give the model rich and scope capabilities where it can do things that the user really wants, aiding and enabling them, and even where the human can still verify the work that it's doing.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: This framing is what turns agent experience into less of a question of the model and more of a question of context, capability, and overall self-improvement.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Let the agent do the heavy lifting and only burden the user with thinking about their use case and writing a prompt.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Someone would feed it a half-baked description from a customer call or maybe a Notion page, and the agent would just start going and build the entire workflow end-to-end, but very confidently it would tell the user that everything it did was right, but neither the user nor the agent could explain what the workflow actually did.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: The agent never really said that it's not sure.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So for example, instead of one create step of this workflow to call over and over and just praying that the agent assembled it right in the pipeline, I built tools that understood how our internal dashboard or our product works.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And after each step, the agent gets contextual guidance on what actually comes next, with certain tools even chaining automatically like this one, rather than the agent having to guess or think about what is right versus being told what's right.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Now the agent doesn't get to freelance the parts that we know are true.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And because the tools only let pipelines take the shape that we as the engineers and the product wanted, the human could follow exactly what happened and we could explain the agent's outputs to downstream users of this MCP tool.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So to avoid auto mode, you don't hand your agent an API.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Thinking back to auto mode, the agent was confidently wrong and no one could see it.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And the human could follow what the agent did.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: When the outcome itself that the agent is trying to build goes wrong, who can tell?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: For example, if we had a really bad schema, or maybe the user didn't really specify the actual use case, how can we tell that the agent did something wrong?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: The agent itself is very confidently wrong and the uncertainty that the agent has is completely invisible.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: The agent also has to surface its own uncertainty.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Basically, in our evals, we started failing the agent for building any shaky assumptions, and we gave our harness prompt guidance to use the ask user question tools, et cetera, that Claude Code and other frontier harnesses offer instead of guessing.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And judgment doesn't live in the agent alone.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: This entire pipeline is still overseen by the user, and the confidence and the reasoning of the agent was then outputted as basically prompt guidance in the MCP.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: The agent basically satisfies what you wrote and not the outcome that you wanted.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And then an agent that passed the test by reward hacking or hiding what it did.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And underneath, they're basically one shape where the agent had more autonomy and more access than the human could verify.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So building the pipeline, generating the schema, and pulling in the right context is where the agent is most powerful and where a mistake is the cheapest because the human is right there.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Where the agent operates, it earns trust by being verifiable, correct, and building trust in service of the user.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And we even asked our sales team and other people on the team to basically export their Claude code sessions to understand how the model was behaving, where humans overrode the agent, where confidence of the model ran low, and where it asked questions.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And so one thing that kind of told me that we were doing something right with these improvements is I never explicitly told the sales team to use the agent to build pipelines, but rather I just exposed it in our Claude enterprise as reducto tools.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So when an agent's experience was built really in service of the users that were using it, we weren't pushing people directly toward it, and rather they reached for it and actually started using it as a company-wide resource.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Overall, a few months ago, I would have told you that agent first means that you have the best model, the best inference, speed, or intelligence of the model.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: To some extent, the agent doesn't go first.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And to build for agent experience means you have to consider the agent being in the loop with the people who have to answer for the work downstream.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So it's not just what does the agent connect to.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Everyone's agent connects to everything nowadays, and Claude can make a new connector for you immediately.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: But beyond that, it's when your agent is really confidently wrong, who finds out and how fast do they find out?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

entities.name: 智能体体验 (agent experience)
entities.how_described: 本集提出智能体优先软件的三个模式中，正确答案是『服务用户的智能体体验』：给智能体丰富且范围明确的能力，同时让人仍能验证它做的工作。

evidence.quote: And lastly, the bucket that I think wins here is agent experience in service of the user.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: This framing is what turns agent experience into less of a question of the model and more of a question of context, capability, and overall self-improvement.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

entities.name: MCP
entities.how_described: 本集讲 Reducto 删掉了第一个 MCP server——把每个 API 都包成工具的大文件——换成更少但承载真实工作结构的工具，让正确路径成为最简单的路径。

evidence.quote: So the clear move to get here for us was an MCP server.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: To get some validation for the direction, I threw together an MVP with Claude Code, and every API endpoint that drove our app was given an MCP tool in one massive file.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: The real test happened when I gave the MCP to everyone on the team, and immediately it broke.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: The whole file that we use to talk to the MCP, I deleted the entire thing in one commit.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And because the tools only let pipelines take the shape that we as the engineers and the product wanted, the human could follow exactly what happened and we could explain the agent's outputs to downstream users of this MCP tool.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So the correct path also becomes the simplest path that the MCP can take.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: This entire pipeline is still overseen by the user, and the confidence and the reasoning of the agent was then outputted as basically prompt guidance in the MCP.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: By building for that interface, we were able to also have user satisfaction go up with the MCP because they could really see what was going on.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And so once we reach this point, we focus on instrumentation where every MCP session, the prompts that were sent from the model were logged.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: It flowed back into the long-term guidance that the MCP had overall.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So before they had a customer call, they would use Circleback or Slack and basically learn about the customer and then use the MCP to basically ask them questions about the customer and then build a pipeline for that customer downstream.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

entities.name: 不确定性 (uncertainty)
entities.how_described: 本集认为运行时失败的核心是智能体的不确定性完全不可见，解法是让不确定性清晰可读：用置信度分数、边界框反馈给模型，奖励提问、惩罚硬猜。

evidence.quote: The agent itself is very confidently wrong and the uncertainty that the agent has is completely invisible.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So everything that we did to fix this basically came down to one change which was making uncertainty really legible.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: But that's just the outcome uncertainty.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: The agent also has to surface its own uncertainty.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: So what happens if you make the uncertainty basically a bit more legible and you keep the final judgment where it can actually be accountable in the hands of the human, then that one clarifying question does the work of all three, giving the model context, capability, and also adding a human in the loop to actually build that judgment and verify things as well.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00
